operations: split the ambiguously adopted assistant change out of the ruling: the user's design stays a mechanism marked as the user's ruling, the implemented-but-unconfirmed change becomes an open naming its proposer and the approval's unclear scope
no merge of the open into the mechanism until a user fact adopts the change explicitly

result.reason: The body mixes a user ruling with an assistant change the user approved only ambiguously, and its bare current choice and confirmed hide that; the ruling stays a mechanism with its attribution, the unconfirmed change is an open that names the proposer and what was and was not approved, and the category test decides the split — not the number of actors.

examples.review: Reconstructed case with pre-revision facts, not an exact replay. Mixed actors alone do not split, and the proposal, adoption and implementation stages of one design stay on one identity; the split is by decision object, made only because the interface detail and the lifecycle would be read and changed apart and the compound body left the makers and approval scopes unassignable. The cited user approval behind the parent's confirmed was of a different change and adopts nothing here; the assistant's later choice does not override the user's design, and that design is never retired as disposable implementation detail. Anchors in the read-only production copy: the user's proposal F1841 (T1032#E1) admitted as K386@1037; the approval F1978 is of the spec and tickets (F1966, F1977), not of F1841 directly; implementation F2176 (T1166#E3..E4); the assistant's proposal F3364 and choice F3395; the user's approval F3390 is of a different change; F4255 negates F3395. The harness seeds one user decision fact per parent, so this round is reviewed against those anchors, not against seeded facts.
